subject: Pilot sourcing framework — hosted / dedicated / private cost recap

Subject: Pilot sourcing framework — hosted / dedicated / private cost recap

Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and asks so we have a clean plan: 

What we heard
- Volume: steady baseline ~200k tokens/day with 5–10x spikes during batch jobs and peak hours (estimated 1.2M tokens on heavy days).
- Latency target: 250ms p50, 800ms p95 (customer-facing chat).
- Security: primary requirement is VPC isolation and tenant-level audit logs; some PII may be stored transiently.
- Compliance: may require data residency controls later (PA/CRA teams will confirm).

What we propose you evaluate (ask from EdgeScale)
1) Hosted API (pay-as-you-go) — fastest onboarding, great for spikes but potentially higher unit cost.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — predictability and lower unit cost for baseline; burst for spikes.
3) Private VPC / on-prem pilote — necessary if procurement requires customer-managed infra and stricter controls.

Next asks for us (by 12/2):
- We will deliver a 3-scenario cost snapshot (hosted per-token, dedicated with reserved commit, private VPC estimate) with assumptions called out.
- Please confirm approximate monthly RPS during peak hour and any absolute hard limits for compute placement (e.g., no public cloud for some datasets).
- Procurement timeline: you mentioned initial pilot approval in ~3 weeks — confirm.

Attaching my raw discovery notes (EdgeScale_Discovery_Notes.pdf). Karthik — can you run a quick sizing + back-of-envelope cost for the three scenarios below? Use a 30-day pilot window as baseline for numbers. Marissa — any objections to proposing a Dedicated trial with a short credit to reduce friction?

Best,
Jordan
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pilot sourcing framework — hosted / dedicated / private cost recap (cost snapshot)

Team — quick back-of-envelope for EdgeScale pilot (30-day window). Assumptions: open model equivalent to 13B, quantized to 4-bit, avg input+output seq length 150 tokens, baseline 6M tokens/month, peak burst to 1.5M/day, required p95 <= 800ms. Pricing math below (rounded):

1) Hosted (pay-as-you-go)
- Unit: $0.0007 per token (generation + prompt combined estimate)
- Monthly cost @6M tokens: $4,200
- Peak-day estimate (1.5M): additional $1,050
- Pros: zero infra ops, instant scaling; Cons: higher marginal cost for steady load

2) Dedicated (reserved commit + burst)
- Reserve: 1 x DGX-equivalent pool (sized for baseline throughput ~50 rps sustained), monthly commit estimate: $18,000 (includes reserved GPU hours + networking).
- Effective unit cost at 6M tokens (amortized): ~$0.0029/token when you account for fixed cost (note: this number improves quickly as tokens increase; at 30M tokens/month it drops under $0.0007/token).
- Burst: allow pay-as-you-go burst at hosted rates or short-term burst pool (adds ~10–20% above commit cost).
- Pros: predictable latency, lower long-run cost for high volume; Cons: higher committed spend for small pilots

3) Private VPC / on-prem estimate
- Initial infra + integration for pilot (1 rack-equivalent + network + setup): CAPEX-like $60k–$90k for 30-day pilot equivalent (we usually propose a hosted proof then migrate to private for production).
- Ops overhead: ongoing SRE support (monthly retainer $6k–$12k).
- Pros: maximum isolation & residency controls; Cons: significant initial outlay and longer procurement.

Recommendations for EdgeScale pilot:
- Offer a 30–45 day Dedicated trial with a limited reserved commit + 50% credits on billed usage for the pilot period. Rationale: keeps performance predictable and shows cost benefits if tokens rise.
- Provide hosted fallback for spikes during pilot (minimize failed requests).

Next steps
- I will export a one-sheet spreadsheet (ES_cost_snapshot.xlsx) with these numbers and the per-token math by scenario.
- Jordan: propose we send the one-sheet and a short call invite for next Wed to walk through.

Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
